today.h: The Index Rebounded, the Market Didn't: Chips Up 2.5% in a 4-of-11 Tape, 10Y Back at 4.95%
today.d: The S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92 as SOXX climbed 2.50% off a bear-market close, but only four of 11 sectors gained and the equal-weight RSP fell 0.33%; the Dow lost 197 points, staples dropped 2.07% and a solid JOLTS print pushed the 10Y up 4bp to 4.95%.
today.c1: A rebound in chips, not in the market. The S&P 500 opened at 7,552.92, never traded below its prior close, peaked at 7,594.61 and finished 27.52 points or 0.36% higher at 7,568.92, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.83% to 25,372.01. The lift came from the AI hardware complex: SOXX rose 2.50% to $465.00, with SanDisk 4.78%, AMD 3.65%, Broadcom 3.07% and Nvidia 2.29%, one session after the PHLX Semiconductor Index closed 21.9% below its 10/6 high and in its second bear market since June. Underneath, the tape was narrow: only four of 11 sectors advanced, the equal-weight RSP fell 0.33% and the Dow lost 197.26 points to 51,786.72 as Sherwin-Williams -3.26% and Home Depot -2.20% offset Microsoft +2.74%. Staples -2.07% and materials -2.01% led the seven decliners. Rates did the rest: September JOLTS showed 7.5 million openings and a 3.4% hiring rate, the 10Y par yield rose 4bp to 4.95%, the 30Y 4bp to 5.32%, the dollar index firmed 0.09% and December gold settled 0.7% lower at $3,940.40. Oil fell a second day — WTI -0.38% to $96.09, Brent -1.12% to $103.60 — and the VIX eased 1.51% to 20.83 with the midterm vote still being counted.
today.c4:
• The breadth tell: the S&P rose 0.36% while the equal-weight RSP fell 0.33% and seven of 11 sectors lost — the index is being carried, not confirmed.
  • The rate tell: JOLTS at 7.5 million openings lifted the whole curve with crude falling, which is why the dollar, gold and the defensives all leaned the same way.
  • The oil tell: Brent's first settle below $104 since 10/7 leaves the war premium $14.04 smaller in two sessions, and energy at -0.85% is now a drag rather than the hedge.
  • The gates: a midterm count still unresolved, refunding 11/4 at 8:30 a.m. ET, payrolls 11/6, the FOMC 12/8-9 — and AMD's 7% after-hours gain is the first read on whether the chip bid survives its own earnings.

qtd.h: Q4's Ledger: the Record Is 3.3% Away, Tech 9.8% Lower, the Average Stock 5.4% Higher

qtd.c1: Q4 is one month and twenty-four sessions old, and its ledger is a rotation rather than a drawdown. The S&P 500 is 82.62 points below its 9/30 base at 7,568.92, or -1.08%, and 3.30% below the record close of 7,818.93 it set on 10/6; the Dow is +1.73% at 51,786.72 and the Nasdaq -5.54% at 25,372.01. Rates have helped rather than hurt: the 10Y is 34bp lower at 4.95%, the 30Y 32bp lower at 5.32% and the 2Y 27bp lower at 4.61%, even with a December hike 79% priced. Gold is -5.88% at $3,940.40 and bitcoin -6.92% at $77,775.
qtd.c4:
• The quarter's defining number is the gap, not the level: S&P -1.08% against RSP +5.40%, a 6.49-point win for the average stock in 24 sessions.
  • The quarter's two decliners are the AI trade: technology is giving back part of a 22.60% year, communications is extending a 13.83% loss, and staples, utilities and health lead the nine gainers.
  • The 10Y's 34bp decline has run alongside a 79% December-hike probability, so duration has been paid despite the Fed, not because of it.
  • Still owed: refunding 11/4, payrolls 11/6 and the FOMC 12/8-9, with the 10/6 record 3.30% above the close.
